$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: Mud Where Ice Should Be

goal.text: Find your footing on the flats, and help the guide before the tide.

steps.label: Cross the shell-bank to the burrow town
Help a traveler on the flats
Learn a new way to listen

plate.narration: Gray-green mudflats stretch toward a hazy sea. Silt banks, salt pools and crooked drowned trees. Out here the ground changes its mind with every tide.

flats.narration: Brackish water curls around ridges of mud. A small figure on a shell-bank stops you before your boots sink. "Shells, not that patch! Welcome to the Saltrot." The guide is a Skupper, with bright eyes and strong front fins. "Silt has buried my town's front door, and the tide turns soon. Help me open it, and I will show you the flats."

variants.text: Behind you, Old Ossley poles his flat boat back into the channel.
Behind you, the fold still hums with cold glacier air.
Behind you, the linked fold carries the cloud whales' distant song.

shells.narration: The guide skips ahead toward a humped island of mud. "Mud has opinions," she says. "Skip where I skip, or poke before you step." Fiddler crabs wave their one big claw in rows, like a crowd at a parade.

shells_a.narration: You copy the guide's skips: one big hop, two small ones, one wobble. A fiddler crab waves its claw at every hop. The guide says it is counting. Counting what, she does not say.

shells_b.narration: The guide hands you a long pole. Poke, listen for the squelch, step. Where the pole sinks, go around. A fiddler crab holds up its claw, as if to say, wrong way.

shells_a_check.prompt: Skip along in the guide's footprints. Light feet, and no stopping!

shells_b_check.prompt: Poke, listen and pick the firmest shells to step on.

shells_done.narration: You cross the first stretch with dry-ish boots. "Good skipping," says the guide. That is a very high compliment. Behind you, the fiddler crabs wave.

shells_off.narration: One boot sinks to the ankle with a long, rude squelch. The guide pulls you out by the sleeve. The mud keeps your sock. "It does that," she says. "Mud likes socks."

shell_path.narration: The last steps up are three kinds of shell: whelk, cockle and oyster. "Wrong order, and they roll," says the guide. She tells a different bit of the order to each hero. "Put it together. I am a guide, not a parrot."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then step on the shells in order.
clues: The guide says: start on the whelk.
The oyster comes last, because it is the biggest.
The cockle is somewhere in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: Whelk, cockle, oyster. Every shell holds.

onFailure.narration: A shell rolls, and the guide catches your sleeve. "Scenic route," she laughs.

onAssisted.narration: You lay the clues side by side, and the order is clear.

town.narration: A round hatch in the mud is the front door of Tidepocket, the guide's burrow town. Cold gray silt is piled on it like icing. Tapping comes from below. "My grandmother," says the guide. "She is not patient." The tide will not wait either.

town_a_check.prompt: Grab a shell scoop and dig until the hatch pops free!

town_b_check.prompt: Plan a trench so the silt slides away, not back onto the hatch.

town_brace.narration: Your thornguard plants both feet and braces the sagging hatch frame, so the silt cannot slump back. Everyone else digs around those sturdy legs.

town_brace_check.prompt: Dig hard while your thornguard holds the hatch frame steady.

town_done.narration: The hatch swings up with a pop and a puff of warm air. Skuppers pour out in a cheerful line, rubbing their eyes.

town_off.narration: The silt slumps back over half the hatch. A Skupper child pops out through the gap anyway, like a cork. Everyone is muddier than you hoped, but the hatch stays open. Skuppers pour out, rubbing their eyes.

hatch_party.narration: The whole town blinks in the sunlight, and everybody wants help at once. "Pick a job," says the guide, "and do it loudly." Her grandmother is still climbing the ladder, not patiently.

interaction.cue: Everyone pick a job and help the families out.

options.label: Hand out kelp cakes
options.reaction: A small Skupper takes a cake in each fin and another in her mouth.

options.label: Sweep silt off the steps
options.reaction: The steps shine. A crab inspects them and approves.

options.label: Cheer for the grandmother
options.reaction: The grandmother says, "About time," again, but she smiles.

stages: The steps are clear and the cakes are going around.

onSuccess.narration: The grandmother steps out last, gives you a damp hug and says, "About time."

onFailure.narration: The grandmother steps out last, gives you a damp hug and says, "About time."

silt.narration: Now you can see the silt properly. It is pale and gray and cold. "Saltrot mud is brown and warm," says the guide. "This came down the river from the cold north. It buries my paths overnight. Today I need hands." A Skupper child says it tastes like old pennies. Nobody asks how she knows.

local.narration: "New silt," says the guide, pointing at a pale stripe. "It covered the path overnight." Beyond it, a traveler waves both arms. She left a bag on a shell-bank that is slowly flooding. Gulls circle it, because it smells of fish. How will you help?

bag.narration: You line up along the shell-bank, each on a firm shell, ready to pass the bag. It smells very strongly of fish. The gulls are extremely interested.

path.narration: You follow the guide and lay empty shells along the firm route. The traveler hops on one foot to keep her boots dry. "Trust a path once," says the guide. "Then look again."

bag_check.prompt: Pass the bag hand to hand without stepping off the firm shells.

path_check.prompt: Pick the firmest shells and lay a route the traveler can follow.

traveler_done.narration: The bag arrives dry. The traveler hugs it and gives you a dried fish, which you will not be eating, and a small river charm. "For luck on soft ground." She hops away, the gulls following in a hopeful cloud.

traveler_off.narration: A wave slaps the shells and wets the bag. The traveler squeaks and grabs it herself. "Still mostly dry," she says. "Mostly." The guide scratches a note in the mud with one fin: look again.

puff.narration: Something round bobs past in the reeds. It is a young Skupper, puffed up to three times her size. "My cousin," groans the guide. "She puffs when she is startled." Her spines stick out like a very round hedgehog. She cannot get down.

puff_a.prompt: Throw the rope loop around her tail fin and tow her in. Mind the spines!

puff_b.prompt: Hum a slow, calm tune until she lets her breath out.

puff_song.narration: Your songkeeper sings a slow song about the tide going out. The cousin's spines droop, little by little. Everyone else keeps the rope ready and stays out of poking range.

puff_song_check.prompt: Sing the tide song softly, and keep her calm until she shrinks.

puff_done.narration: The cousin lets out a squeaky sigh and shrinks, like a small round bagpipe. "Thank you. This morning I saw old posts upriver, where the pale silt starts, standing in dry mud." The guide goes quiet. Her family sends a warm honeycake after you.

puff_off.narration: The cousin startles at a gull and puffs even bigger. The guide pokes her gently with a pole until she sighs and shrinks. "Sorry. This morning I saw old posts upriver, where the pale silt starts, standing in dry mud." The guide goes quiet. Her family sends a warm honeycake after you.

ossley.narration: "Posts," says the guide. "Later." A flat boat runs aground in the channel with a soft thump. A frogfolk boatman peers over the side. It is Old Ossley, the ferry man. His boat is full of crates for Tidepocket, and the tide is lapping at his keel. "Hands?"

variants.text: He winks at you. "Same river, same fare, eh?"

ossley_a.prompt: Make a chain and pass the crates ashore before the tide climbs.

ossley_b.prompt: Slide planks under the keel so the boat floats free.

ossley_done.narration: The last crate lands as the water reaches the keel. Ossley floats free and catches a sliding crate of kelp with his tongue, without looking. "When you want to go upriver, I am your frog." He pays you five coins. "Honest work, honest pay."

ossley_off.narration: The tide wins the race. Ossley bails with a bucket while you carry the last crates through knee-deep water. Everything arrives, a little damp. "When you want to go upriver, I am your frog," he says, and pays you three coins. "For the wet ones."

lamp_line.narration: Tidepocket's lamps need oil before dark, and the hatch ladder is steep and slippery. "One jar at a time," says the guide. "Catch it, pass it, and do not drop it."

interaction.cue: Catch the jar, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: The last jar reaches the bottom. Below, the lamps pop alight, and Tidepocket glows like a pot of warm honey.

onFailure.narration: One jar slips, and a Skupper child catches it with her tail. "I meant to do that."

onAssisted.narration: You and the guide pass the jars in a steady line, and the lamps pop alight below.

camp.narration: The families press a hot kelp cake into every hand. "Diggers eat first," says the guide. You rest on top of the burrow while the tide comes in, silver and quiet. Two travelers wade toward you in Riftseeker clasps. One has far too many tails to count.

camp_story.narration: The guide's grandmother settles on a shell. "In the old stories there is a bridge, and a door, and a rule: show the bank, never the stone." She squints at the guide. "You know it? Good." Then she tells it again, shorter.

camp_gift.narration: The grandmother breaks the honeycake into tiny pieces and hands them down the line. Everyone gets one crumb. She keeps the smallest. "Good manners," she says. Then she tells her bridge story, with its rule: show the bank, never the stone.

camp_boots.narration: You rinse your boots in a tide pool. A small crab climbs out of the left one and glares. "Mine," says the guide, and puts it on her head. Nearby, the grandmother finishes a story with a rule: show the bank, never the stone.

lesson.narration: Seren Wisp, the kitsune from the glacier, is traveling with a young manticore named Pip Thistledown. "I find what has moved," says Pip, unrolling a muddy map. "The pale silt starts upriver. I need good ears." Seren asks you to hum the hall note and listen. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune."

variants.text: Seren Wisp and Pip Thistledown are here too, checking another moved route. Pip unrolls a muddy map. "The pale silt starts upriver. I need good ears." Seren asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before.

hum.narration: Seren sets a pebble in the mud. "Every rift hums," she says. "Some hum back when someone who can answer is near." Far across the flats, something hums faintly, like a bee in a bucket. How will you find where it comes from?

hum_chime.narration: You ring the Listening Chime near the mud. The note rises, then bends north, as if something far away answered in a slightly different voice. Pip sticks out his tongue and draws an arrow.

hum_chime_check.prompt: Follow the bend in the chime's note across the flats.

hum_a_check.prompt: Hum the hall note together, then hold still and listen for the flats to hum back.

hum_b_check.prompt: Walk the flats and mark every spot where the hum goes quiet.

hum_star.narration: Your starweaver listens the way Seren taught, and the flats hum a little louder in answer. Everyone else keeps still and watches the mud.

hum_star_check.prompt: Answer the hum with attune, and follow it across the mud.

hum_done.narration: Under the mud, a low note hums back from the cold north. Pip writes it down and underlines it twice. "That is where the pale silt starts," says Seren, "or near it." The guide looks upriver, and her tall crest folds flat.

hum_off.narration: The note hides in the squelch, but Seren's long ears catch it: a low hum from the cold north. Pip underlines it twice. "That is where the pale silt starts," says Seren, "or near it." The guide looks upriver, and her tall crest folds flat.

poles.narration: The guide drags over a bundle of reed poles. "Every morning I mark the safe route. This morning it is under silt. Nobody crossing tomorrow should have to guess." A Tidepocket weaver waves a roll of bright cloth. "Three coins, and every pole will shine."

poles_a_check.narration: The guide leads you along the firm shells while you plant the poles. She wiggles each one before you move on. Not one wiggles back.

poles_b_check.narration: You tie reed flags to the poles. Pip checks them from the next shell-bank and waves both arms. Even he can see where to go.

poles_buy.narration: The weaver cuts the cloth into strips, and you tie one on every pole. In the low light they shine like tiny lanterns. The weaver looks very pleased with herself.

poles_done.narration: The poles stand in a long straight line, like thin sentries. The guide walks it with her eyes closed, without one wobble. "Silt or no silt, anyone can follow this."

trail.narration: Pip lays his map on a reed drum. The pale stripe runs upriver, getting wider. "Follow it, and we find where it starts. The cousin saw posts. I want to see posts." "Will you come?" Seren asks the guide. She folds her fins. "To the bank. Not past it."

trail_charm.narration: Your river charm warms when you step on firm ground and goes cool over soft. You start walking by temperature. The guide decides not to be offended that a pebble is better at her job.

trail_charm_check.prompt: Follow the charm along the stripe: warm for firm, cool for soft.

trail_wing.narration: A winged friend rises over the flats and follows the pale stripe like a gray ribbon. Everyone below keeps their eyes on the flier.

trail_a_check.prompt: Keep one foot on each color of mud, and do not lose the stripe.

trail_b_check.prompt: Work out where firm ground ends and soft silt begins.

trail_wing_check.prompt: Fly along the stripe and call the way down to the walkers.

trail_done.narration: The pale stripe grows wider and colder, a gray road through the brown. Ahead, it climbs a long, low rise, as if the land were holding its breath. Behind you, every fiddler crab lifts its claw at once.

trail_off.narration: You lose the stripe twice under fresh brown mud and find it again by the squelch. It takes the long way around. Ahead, the pale line climbs a long, low rise. Behind you, every fiddler crab lifts its claw at once.

crabs.narration: The crabs wave together, all facing the river. "They do not do that," says the guide. "They wave by the tide, and the tide is hours away." Her crest stands straight up. "They know something we do not. Find out. Fast."

crabs_a.prompt: Count the waves and watch the water mark on a pole. Do they line up?

crabs_b.prompt: Scramble up the slippery rise before the next wave of crabs.

crabs_leap.narration: Your manticore crouches, wiggles, and leaps high onto the ledge in one bound. Pip's mouth falls open. Everyone below shouts questions, and the manticore shouts back what they see.

crabs_leap_check.prompt: Leap to the ledge, look upriver and call down what you see.

crabs_done.narration: Upriver, water is piling up behind a long gray bar of silt, like a bath with the plug in. "It will come back all at once," you tell the guide. She nods. "Early tide. But that is not what they are waving about." The silt beside you heaves.

crabs_off.narration: You work it out a little late. The crabs run sideways for the high shells, which is also an answer. Upriver, water is piling up behind a long gray bar of silt. "Early tide," says the guide. "But that is not why they ran." The silt beside you heaves.

crab_warn.narration: Two big crabs push up out of the silt, shells clear as windows. "Glassback crabs," whispers the guide. "The cold silt froze their warm mud. Now they want the warm shell-bank you are standing on." One clacks at Pip's map. Pip holds it very high.

crab_fight.narration: The crabs scuttle sideways at you, claws up. They are not wicked, only cold and cross. Hold the shell-bank until they settle.

crab_done.narration: The crabs back off and settle into a warm hollow, glaring at the sky. One leaves a glassy pebble at your feet. "A luckstone," says the guide. "That is a very good-mannered crab." Behind you, the water begins to slide.

crab_rescued.narration: A crab shoves you off the shell-bank, and you sit down in the silt with a squelch. The families bang cooking pots from the hatch, and the crabs scuttle off to a warm hollow, grumbling. Nobody is hurt. Behind you, the water begins to slide.

tide.narration: Up the channel, a gray wall of water slides toward you, quiet as a cat. "The silt piles the water up," says the guide. For the first time she sounds worried. "High shells! Now!"

tide_a.prompt: Run for the high shells, light and fast, and beat the water!

tide_b.prompt: Anchor the rope on a firm shell and hold it while friends wade along.

tide_done.narration: Everyone is across, and Pip counts heads. "Right number," he says. A fiddler crab sits on his head, waving. One last channel lies between you and the high shells, and the water is sliding in.

tide_off.narration: Water fills your boots, cold as a river from the north, which it is. Everyone stays together, soggy and safe. Pip wrings out his map. The guide wrings out Pip. One last channel lies ahead, and the water is sliding in.

tide_dash.narration: The water pulls back from the last channel, then rushes in again, like a giant, rude breath. "Wait for the pull," says the guide. "Then go."

interaction.cue: Go when the water pulls back.

onSuccess.narration: You hop across on dry shells to the high shells.

onFailure.narration: The water gets your boots, but the guide hauls you up by the collar, laughing.

onAssisted.narration: The guide counts the pulls, and you cross on the last one.

lead.narration: From the high shells, you see where the pale stripe ends. The mud has pulled back from a long line of old gray stone, standing in dry ground like the teeth of a giant's comb. "The buried bridge," says the guide quietly. "My folk have a rule. We show the bank. We do not walk on it." Seren nods. "Something moved, and uncovered it."

bridge_ask.narration: The tide slides back out. Pip is already sketching the stone. "Master Orin Vale will want to see this," says Seren. "He studies silt." The guide watches the bridge, not you. What will you do first?

bridge_go.narration: The guide takes a long breath and puffs a little at the edges. "The bank," she says. "I will show you the bank. Not the stone." She hops onto the firmest shell.

bridge_plan.narration: Seren draws the route on Pip's map in three lines. "The firm bank first. The silt second. The stone last, and only from the bank." Pip underlines the word bank. The guide gives a very small nod.

flats_rest.narration: You rest above the tide line while the water goes back out. The guide scratches the day's lesson in the mud. "Look again," she says. When you are ready, she will take you to the bank of the buried bridge.

variants.text: The open fold still hums nearby. It could carry you back to the glacier.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
